france24fr.title: Ouverture des bureaux de vote en Arménie pour les élections législatives
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert dimanche en Arménie pour les élections législatives, un scrutin à valeur de test pour l'orientation pro-européenne du Premier ministre Nikol Pachinian.

france24fr.title: Le pape Léon XIV célèbre une messe à Madrid devant plus d'un million de fidèles
france24fr.description: Quelque 1,2 million de fidèles ont envahi les rues du centre de Madrid, dimanche, pour assister à la messe célébrée par Léon XIV. Lors de cette cérémonie religieuse, le pape a appelé à un renouveau de la foi catholique en Espagne.

france24fr.title: Grâce aux Rafales français, des avions russes interceptés en Lituanie
france24fr.description: Grâce aux Rafales français, des avions russes interceptés en Lituanie.

france24fr.title: Plus de 1,2M de personnes dans les rues de Madrid pour une messe de Léon XIV
france24fr.description: Plus de 1,2 million de personnes se sont rassemblées dimanche matin dans les rues du centre de Madrid pour suivre une messe célébrée par le pape Léon XIV au deuxième jour de sa visite en Espagne, ont annoncé les organisateurs.

france24fr.title: Victoire d'Andreeva, finale NBA et "caverne du Pont-Neuf" : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine : la tenniswoman russe Mirra Andreeva a remporté son premier Roland-Garros face à la Polonaise Maja Chwalinska, les San Antonio Spurs de Victor Wembanyama croisent le fer avec les New York Knicks en finale NBA et la "caverne du Pont-Neuf" de l'artiste JR reste fermée au public en attendant que l'installation soit réparée.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Pérou : duel serré pour un neuvième président en dix ans
france24fr.description: Entre désillusion politique et exaspération face à la criminalité, les Péruviens élisent dimanche leur président, le neuvième en dix ans, dans un duel opposant la conservatrice Keiko Fujimori au candidat de gauche Roberto Sanchez.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Pérou : duel serré entre Sanchez et Fujimori
france24fr.description: Lissell Quiroz, Professeure d'études latino-américaines à CY Cergy Paris Université, est notre invitée.

france24fr.description: Taline Oundjian est en direct d'Erevan.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'équipe iranienne de football attendue au Mexique
france24fr.description: L'équipe iranienne de football est attendue dimanche au Mexique, où se trouve son camp de base pour la Coupe du monde, malgré le refus par les Etats-Unis, où elle doit disputer ses premiers matches, de délivrer des visas à certains membres de son encadrement.

france24fr.title: La commune de Fleurance rend hommage à Lyhanna lors d'une marche blanche
france24fr.description: La petite commune de Fleurance se prépare à rendre hommage dimanche, lors d'une marche blanche, à Lyhanna, collégienne de 11 ans retrouvée morte, sur fond de polémique concernant le traitement judiciaire des plaintes pour viols sur mineurs visant le principal suspect.

france24fr.title: Mirra Andreeva remporte son premier titre en Grand Chelem à Roland-Garros
france24fr.description: La Russe Mirra Andreeva s'est imposée en finale de Roland-Garros samedi contre Maja Chwalińska, la joueuse polonaise issue des qualifications. Âgée de 19 ans, classée numéro 8 mondiale, la vainqueuse remporte ainsi son premier titre en Grand Chelem.

france24fr.title: États-Unis, Mexique, Canada : trois hôtes et trois passions du foot au Mondial 2026
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois dans l'histoire de la Coupe du monde, le Mondial va se dérouler dans trois pays. États-Unis, Mexique et Canada se partagent l'organisation de la compétition phare du football, mais la comparaison s'arrête là : ces nations sont loin d'afficher la même histoire ni le même engouement pour le ballon rond.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : les États-Unis disent avoir abattu deux drones iraniens
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a annoncé samedi soir avoir abattu deux drones d'attaque iraniens qui menaçaient, selon elle, le trafic maritime dans le détroit stratégique d'Ormuz. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Bouygues Telecom, Free et Orange trouvent un accord pour le rachat de SFR
france24fr.description: Les opérateurs Bouygues Telecom, Iliad (Free) et Orange se sont mis d'accord, samedi soir, avec Altice France pour racheter sa filiale SFR. La transaction, d'un montant total de 20,35 milliards d'euros, marque le coup d'envoi d'un nouveau big bang dans le secteur de la téléphonie mobile en France.

nzz.description: Die SP-Politikerin soll für die Partei den Sitz im Ständerat halten. Dafür braucht sie auch bürgerliche Stimmen. Punkten könnte sie dabei als Unternehmerin – wäre da nicht die Nähe ihrer Firma zum Staat.

nzz.description: Bitcoin taumelt, Privatmarkt-Fonds begrenzen Rücknahmen, Nasdaq-Aktien haben einen schwarzen Freitag. Was aussieht wie Einzelereignisse, könnte denselben Ursprung haben: der enorme Kapitalhunger von KI-Firmen.

observador.description: O Papa Leão 14 pede que a religiosidade "não seja um museu do passado" e apela à luta contra o egoísmo. Ainda, António José Seguro e Luís Montenegro já estão juntos no Luxemburgo.

observador.title: O desafio de um dono da bola entre 11 donos do jogo
observador.description: Espanha procura quarta final seguida de grandes provas para esquecer insucesso dos últimos Mundiais dentro de uma identidade de jogo muito própria que ganhou outra projeção com a magia de Lamine.

observador.title: Os Tubarões como peixes no mar onde "nada é impossível"
observador.description: Cabo Verde tornou-se o terceiro país mais pequeno a qualificar-se para o Mundial e vai estrear-se contra a Espanha mas, entre homenagens e condecorações, quer fazer do momento um início e não o fim.

observador.title: Quatro anos depois, onde anda o tal efeito Ronaldo?
observador.description: Chegada de Ronaldo era vista como motor para potenciar Liga e futebol saudita. Na parte local, falhou – e as apostas em Mancini e Hervé Renard também foram ao lado. Agora, Donis procura um "milagre".

observador.title: As "viúvas" da geração de ouro nas mãos de El Loco Bielsa
observador.description: Valverde trocou agressões num treino, Darwin não jogou, Ugarte pouco jogou, Giménez não conseguia jogar. Agora, eles são a base do novo Uruguai sem Suárez, Cavani ou Godín mas com um Mago no banco.

observador.title: Mundial 2026. Faltam quatro dias para o Campeonato do Mundo
observador.description: Depois da vitória contra o Chile no Jamor, Seleção Nacional tem o primeiro dia fechado à comunicação social na Cidade do Futebol e já com o grupo completo. Mundial começa na quinta-feira. Siga aqui.

observador.title: Economia russa conseguirá aguentar mais tempo de guerra?
observador.description: Liliana Reis, especialista em relações internacionais, admite que é a melhor altura para a Europa liderar o apoio à Ucrânia porque diz que a Rússia está frágil e os EUA estão focados no Médio Oriente.

spiegel.title: Trennungsparty: Warum ich das Ende meiner Beziehung gefeiert habe
spiegel.description: Ich habe meine Freunde zum Abschied von meinem Ex eingeladen. Mit Köstlichkeiten und teurem Wein. Am Ende waren alle betrunken ‒ aber das war nicht das Einzige, das mich so glücklich machte.

spiegel.title: Einstein mit Babytragetuch: Schweizer Bewegung fordert mehr Verantwortung von Vätern
spiegel.description: In der Schweiz haben Aktivisten zahlreiche Männer-Denkmäler mit Babytragetüchern ausgestattet – darunter die Statue des Physikgenies Albert Einstein. Die Gruppe fordert mehr Einsatz von Vätern in der Kinderbetreuung.

spiegel.title: AfD: Insider rechnen mit der eigenen Partei ab: »Säuberungsaktionen wie im Totalitarismus«
spiegel.description: »Sektenartige Zustände«: Ein scheidender AfD-Landtagsabgeordneter warnt vor Chaos, sollte die Partei an die Macht kommen, er schreibt von »Goebbels-Methoden« und »Beutegemeinschaften« – was die Brandbriefe auslösen.

spiegel.title: Johann Lafer: Ehefrau Silvia spricht über die Krebserkrankung ihres Mannes
spiegel.description: In einem Interview spricht Silvia Lafer erstmals über den Lymphdrüsenkrebs ihres Mannes – und über einen Satz der Ärzte, der der ganzen Familie Hoffnung gibt.

spiegel.title: Verena Hubertz: Bundesbauministerin hat in Rheinland-Pfalz geheiratet
spiegel.description: Anfang des Jahres brachte sie ihr erstes Kind zur Welt, nun hat die Bauministerin im kleinen Kreis in der Nähe ihres Heimatorts in Rheinland-Pfalz geheiratet.

spiegel.title: Ironman Hamburg: Möglicher Anschlag mit Metallsplittern
spiegel.description: Metallsplitter auf der Straße haben zahlreiche Radfahrer beim Ironman Hamburg ausgebremst. Sportler und lokale Medien befürchten einen Anschlag auf die Großveranstaltung, die Polizei ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Nigeria: 360 Boko-Haram-Geiseln aus Gefangenschaft befreit
spiegel.description: Hunderte Menschen konnten in Nigeria aus der Gefangenschaft der islamistischen Terrorgruppe Boko Haram befreit werden, so das Militär. Zwei Kinder starben demnach, die restlichen Geiseln seien wohlauf.

spiegel.title: Dubai: Zeynab Javadli wird nach Sorgerechtsstreit mit Scheich festgehalten
spiegel.description: Die frühere Sportgymnastin Zeynab Javadli flehte kürzlich auf Instagram um Hilfe, sie fürchtete eine Verhaftung. Nun wird sie nach einem Sorgerechtsstreit mit einem Mitglied der Herrscherfamilie in Dubai festgehalten.

spiegel.title: Tschernobyl: Anlage für abgebrannte Brennelemente von Russland angegriffen
spiegel.description: Eine russische Drohne soll eine Anlage in der Nähe des Atomkraftwerks Tschernobyl getroffen haben. Die Internationale Atomenergiebehörde zeigt sich besorgt, Selenskyj nennt die Attacke »extrem ⁠niederträchtig«.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo XIV. in Spanien: »Mein Herz schlägt so sehr, wirklich!«
spiegel.description: Mehr als 1,2 Millionen Menschen sollen zur Papstmesse am Sonntag in Madrid zusammengekommen sein. Auch viele junge Gläubige feierten Leo XIV. auf seiner Fahrt durch die Stadt.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo in Madrid: Mehr als eine Million Menschen besuchen Messe
spiegel.description: Laut den Organisatoren haben sich am Sonntag rund 1,2 Millionen Menschen zu einem Gottesdienst mit Papst Leo in Madrid versammelt. Vor seiner Ankunft zog der Papst einen Vergleich zu Bad Bunny.

spiegel.title: Israel: Ein Toter und mehrere Verletzte bei Angriff nahe Westjordanland
spiegel.description: Nahe dem Westjordanland sind mehrere Menschen bei einem mutmaßlichen Terroranschlag verletzt worden, eine Person wurde getötet. Unterdessen sorgt Israels Vorgehen in dem besetzten Gebiet weiter für Kritik – auch in Deutschland.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik: Owen Ansah verbessert deutschen 100-Meter-Rekord auf 9,98 Sekunden
spiegel.description: Vor zwei Jahren blieb Owen Ansah über die 100 Meter als erster Deutscher unter zehn Sekunden. Nun brach er seinen eigenen Rekord, dieses Mal brauchte er nur 9,98 Sekunden. Schneller war in diesem Jahr noch kein Europäer.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Vier Verdächtige nach Haspa-Einbruch von 2023 in Haft
spiegel.description: Zweieinhalb Jahre nach dem Einbruch in eine Hamburger Sparkassenfiliale wurde nun die Höhe der Beute bekannt: 1,95 Millionen Euro. Vier Verdächtige sind mittlerweile in Haft.

spiegel.title: SPD: Andreas Bovenschulte warnt Regierung vor zu hohem Reformtempo
spiegel.description: »Kommunikative Fehler« und schlechtes Erwartungsmanagement: Bremens Regierungschef Andreas Bovenschulte übt im SPIEGEL-Interview harte Kritik an Schwarz-Rot. Und droht mit der Macht des Bundesrats.

spiegel.title: Kontogebühren: Jeder Vierte zahlt laut Umfrage über 100 Euro für das Girokonto
spiegel.description: Die jährlichen Gebühren summieren sich, manche Bankkunden zahlen laut Umfrage eines Vergleichsportals sogar mehr als 200 Euro. Bei einer Bankengruppe zahlen Kunden besonders viel.

spiegel.title: Simone Biles: Olympiastar musste in Klinik
spiegel.description: Simone Biles gilt als eine der besten Turnerinnen der Geschichte. Nun machte sie bei Instagram öffentlich, dass sie einen schweren medizinischen Notfall erlitten hat.

spiegel.title: Frieden durch Käse - Alles Gute vom SPIEGEL
spiegel.description: Zwei Franzosen überwinden Grenzen mit Essen. Die Deutschen machen weniger Müll. Und die besten veganen Würstchen des Sommers. Die guten Nachrichten der Woche.

elpais.title: El Papa, en una misa multitudinaria en Madrid: “Nadie puede arrodillarse ante el Señor y despreciar al hermano”

elpais.description: Madrid recibe al Papa sin especial sobresalto, con más paciencia de la prevista y menos épica de la anunciada

elpais.title: Discurso potente del papa León XIV con carga política en su primer día de visita en España
elpais.description: El Pontífice ha abordado la polarización con frases dirigidas a la ultraderecha y se ha comprometido a luchar contra los casos de abusos de la Iglesia

elpais.title: El Gobierno deja a medias su proyecto laicista tras ocho años de roces y pactos con los obispos
elpais.description: El balance de la relación con la Iglesia de los Ejecutivos de Sánchez muestra avances en neutralidad religiosa y cesiones del episcopado, pero también compromisos abandonados

elpais.description: El denunciado, de origen italiano, está fugado desde 2024 y la justicia rechaza emitir una orden de captura internacional: “Mañana saldrá que le ha hecho esto a otras y se podía haber evitado”

elpais.title: Objetivo: proteger al presidente
elpais.description: Sánchez y su entorno se esfuerzan por cortar la línea del ‘caso Leire Díez’ en Santos Cerdán como único responsable. El Ejecutivo está cada vez más molesto con una UCO “descontrolada” y en plena guerra interna dentro de la Guardia Civil

Luis de la Fuente no tiene dudas. Él es el hombre. El ‘9′ de la Roja. Un futbolista distinto. Conversamos con él en San Sebastián

nyt.description: After a judge’s ruling, there was a sense of renewed hope that immigration applications that were put on hold would move forward. But how soon that would happen was unknown.

nyt.description: Israeli authorities described the shootings as a terrorist attack. Hamas, the Palestinian militant group, praised the assault, but did not claim responsibility.

nyt.description: The president has not yet endorsed Representative Mike Collins or Derek Dooley, a former football coach, in the race to challenge the Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff.

nyt.title: How to Watch the 2026 Tony Awards

nyt.description: A player from Haiti’s 1974 World Cup team, the last to qualify for the tournament, met with the co-captain of this year’s squad in South Florida.

npr.description: The crowd cheered and shouted "This is the youth of the pope!" as Pope Leo arrived for Mass at a central Madrid plaza. It's the first papal visit to Spain in 15 years.

npr.description: In South Africa and Mozambique, health care providers say cancellation or redirection of U.S. PEPFAR funding under the Trump administration have already endangered vulnerable people and cost lives.

npr.description: Young Indians frustrated by unemployment and exam scandals are rallying behind an unusual symbol: the cockroach. NPR's Diaa Hadid reports from New Delhi.

new-sci.title: Hearing loss is bad for the whole body – but new treatments are coming
new-sci.description: From dementia to heart attacks, hearing loss has been linked to a wide range of effects across the body, and the condition is on the rise. Fortunately, we're learning how best to safeguard this crucial sense and how we might be able to reverse the damage

new-sci.title: Cuts to US ocean programme will hinder monitoring of El Niño and AMOC

new-sci.title: Flood of AI 'garbage' is pushing open-source developers to the limit
new-sci.description: The modern world depends on open-source software maintained by volunteers, but the added demands of checking and fixing AI-written submissions are causing some to burn out and quit

new-sci.title: A chromosome from a frozen rat has been resurrected inside mice
new-sci.description: Mice that contain cells with an added rat chromosome have been created by scientists. The next step is to try this with frozen elephant tissue – and if that works, the team will try it with frozen mammoths

new-sci.title: Everyone is Lying to You for Money is a must-watch exposé of crypto
new-sci.description: Actor Ben McKenzie explores the world of crypto in an entertaining documentary that doesn't shy away from calling out those who have promoted the currency

new-sci.description: A seemingly simple set of rules kicks off a kind of mathematical magic trick, which has kept great minds busy since the 1930s. Columnist Jacob Aron explores the origins of the Collatz conjecture, why it is so addictive to mathematicians and whether AI could help us solve it once and for all

new-sci.title: Escher: The paradoxical artist beloved by mathematicians
new-sci.description: A new retrospective of M.C. Escher’s work opens this week. Explore some of his most mind-bending, mathematically inspired works here

new-sci.description: Parents report loving their partners less within the first year of having a child, but that doesn't mean the feeling is permanent or inevitable

new-sci.title: Mysterious ‘cold blob’ in the Atlantic suggests the AMOC is weakening
new-sci.description: A patch of ocean south-east of Greenland is the only place on Earth that is cooling, and it could be a sign that the warm water "conveyor belt" in the Atlantic is slowing down

new-sci.title: How Rachel Carson's Silent Spring changed the world in 1962
new-sci.description: Rachel Carson’s look at the dire effects of industrial and agricultural pollution birthed the modern environmental movement when it was first published – and remains as crucial a read today, finds Rowan Hooper

new-sci.title: The looming El Niño could be bad – but much worse is to come
new-sci.description: Global warming will amplify the impacts of El Niño events, and could also make them much stronger and more far-reaching

new-sci.description: A glacier could have carried the giant sandstone at the centre of Stonehenge southwards from north-east Scotland, but this scenario appears unlikely

phys-org.title: Autonomous AI screening flags unreliable Lyme test results, boosting sensitivity to 95.7%
phys-org.description: Computational point-of-care sensors can significantly improve access to diagnostics by enabling rapid patient testing outside centralized medical facilities. These tests rely on machine learning models to make diagnostic predictions, but such inference models are susceptible to hallucinations and may produce erroneous outcomes. As a result, their limited reliability has partially hindered the broader adoption of computational sensors in health care settings.

phys-org.title: First nonrepeating biological clock discovered in C. elegans guides growth
phys-org.description: Imagine a train parked at the station. Passengers climb aboard and find their seats. Conductors move up and down the aisles, checking tickets. But there's a problem—the engineer's watch is broken. As a result, the doors never close, the whistle never sounds, and the train never starts. Something similar occurs in cells when developmental timing is disrupted. phys-org.title: Hidden protein switch controls photosynthesis as light conditions change
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered a previously unknown regulatory mechanism in plant photosynthesis in the unicellular green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. It helps plants adapt to changes in light conditions. The results, published in the journal Nature Plants, show how a crucial protein interaction at the interface between photosystems I and II controls the photosynthetic machinery.

phys-org.title: Machine learning uncovers 1,750 quakes tracing 250-kilometer edge of Alaska microplate
phys-org.description: Thousands of small earthquakes, detected for the first time by a machine-learning process, reveal the distinct, razor-sharp edge of the Yakutat microplate as it subducts beneath the North American plate.

phys-org.title: Black teachers improve outcomes for all students, but the profession remains largely white
phys-org.description: Having Black teachers and other educators of color improves students' classroom experiences, research shows. They often serve as role models, set high academic expectations and teach material that connects to students' lives outside of schools.

phys-org.title: Medieval pandemic left a hidden legacy in Europe's oldest trees
phys-org.description: A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences demonstrates how radiocarbon dating can reveal the maximum lifespan of Mediterranean hardwoods, uncovering hidden links between human history and long-term ecosystem dynamics. By analyzing mature and ancient oak trees across Italy, researchers found that a millennium of age is attainable from the Mediterranean coast to mountain environments.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Why are white-Black marriage rates so low?
phys-org.description: Americans rarely marry outside of their race or class in a nation where residential segregation is relatively common. It is a dynamic widely viewed as a contributing factor to income inequality and intergenerational social mobility.

phys-org.title: 120,000-year-old European fallow deer—tracing the loss of genetic diversity
phys-org.description: European fallow deer have faced a dramatic loss of genetic diversity since the last interglacial period. This was revealed by 120,000-year-old fossils from central Germany's Neumark-Nord site in Saxony-Anhalt, analyzed by researchers from the University of Potsdam, the MONREPOS Research Center and Museum in Neuwied, and Leiden University. Their results have been published in the journal iScience. Modern fallow deer thus represent just a fraction of their Ice Age ancestors' variety. The

phys-org.title: Ever seen a cave cricket? Australia now has three new species of these spindly, spider-like creatures
phys-org.description: When you picture a cave, you probably think of an environment devoid of life. But for most caves on Earth, this couldn't be further from the truth.

phys-org.title: Infrastructure for African mines destroying forests at 34 times the rate of the mines themselves
phys-org.description: Industrial-scale mining in Africa to support global supply chains is leading to unprecedented deforestation across the continent, with 34 hectares of forest removed for every single hectare of active mine site.

phys-org.title: AI-generated compounds hit specific cell types and outperform conventional screening
phys-org.description: The classical drug discovery paradigm begins with a known molecular target: a protein whose modulation is expected to reverse the course of a disease. However, in many pathologies, such a target does not always exist or is not sufficiently characterized.

phys-org.title: Previously unknown detoxification pathway for chloromethane revealed
phys-org.description: Chloromethane is a gas that is toxic to humans and contributes to the depletion of the ozone layer. It is produced during the combustion of coal, biomass and other raw materials. Natural sources such as algae, plants and fungi also release it. A research team led by biologist Prof. Julia Kurth from the University of Münster has discovered and characterized a previously unknown enzyme system in anaerobic bacteria of the species Acetobacterium dehalogenans. This system converts the gas into nontox

phys-org.title: Mount Etna eruptions reveal carbon dioxide and water can trigger separate explosive paths
phys-org.description: The plumbing systems of volcanoes are vast and complex. But they aren't consistent, even in the same volcano. A Cornell-led collaboration found very different mechanisms behind two historic eruptions of Mount Etna in Italy. Understanding these dynamics—combined with the techniques that revealed them—can help geologists assess the risk of future eruptions.

phys-org.title: Africa's climate crisis is a legal crisis too: What are states' duties under human rights law?
phys-org.description: A landmark climate case is being heard by the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights. The request was brought by the Pan African Lawyers Union and other African civil society organizations. They've asked the court to issue advice on what responsibilities African governments have to protect their countries against the climate crisis and move away from an economy that harms the environment.

phys-org.title: Predictive surrogates could cut quantum computing measurement overhead by more than 99.97%
phys-org.description: Quantum computers, systems that process information leveraging quantum mechanical effects, have the potential of outperforming classical computers on some tasks. Despite their potential, the use of these systems remains very limited, due to their high cost and other challenges that have so far prevented their large-scale fabrication.

phys-org.title: Sweet basil carbon dots show potential for sustainable agriculture
phys-org.description: What if a common herb found in the kitchen could help farmers grow healthier crops? As the global population grows and agriculture faces increasing environmental challenges, scientists are searching for innovative ways to improve crop productivity while reducing reliance on chemical inputs.

phys-org.title: Smart surfaces face zero gravity test in boiling heat experiments
phys-org.description: A research team led by Davoud Jafari at the University of Twente, in collaboration with the University of Pisa, has completed a series of parabolic flight experiments to investigate advanced smart surfaces under rapidly changing gravity conditions. Conducted aboard the Air Zero G aircraft operated by Novespace, the campaign integrated additive manufacturing, boiling heat transfer and electric field control into a single experimental platform as part of the #SmartSkin project.

phys-org.title: MUSE maps spiral galaxy W2246f, uncovering old core and ongoing star formation across disk
phys-org.description: Astronomers have employed the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) on the Very Large Telescope (VLT) to perform deep spectroscopic observations of a peculiar spiral galaxy known as W2246f. Results of the observational campaign, published May 27 on the pre-print server arXiv, offer new insights into how this galaxy evolved and shed more light on its nature.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.
